# Detective Bots LLM Simulation
[](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) **Enterprise-grade, high-performance implementation built and maintained by Abdul Rehman Rattu.** [Overview](#overview) • [Key Features](#key-features) • [Installation & Usage](#quickstart--deployment) • [Author & Maintainer](#author--maintainer)
--- A multi-agent simulation framework that benchmarks four large language models — GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, Gemini-2.0-Flash, and Gemini-2.0-Flash-Lite — across 40 fully autonomous detective mystery games. Five AI agents, each embodying one of the Big Five (OCEAN) personality traits, interrogate each other through structured questioning, strategic deception, and majority-vote reasoning to identify a hidden killer. --- ## Table of Contents - [Overview](#overview) - [Key Features](#key-features) - [System Architecture](#system-architecture) - [Agent Personalities](#agent-personalities) - [Game Flow](#game-flow) - [Models Benchmarked](#models-benchmarked) - [Results Summary](#results-summary) - [Visualizations](#visualizations) - [Topic Modeling Analysis](#topic-modeling-analysis) - [Project Structure](#project-structure) - [Setup and Installation](#setup-and-installation) - [Running the Simulation](#running-the-simulation) - [Running the Analysis](#running-the-analysis) - [Output Files](#output-files) - [Technical Stack](#technical-stack) - [Report](#report) - [Contact](#contact) --- ## Overview This project implements a closed-loop, multi-agent conversational system where five AI agents operate simultaneously in a detective scenario. Each agent is assigned a distinct behavioral profile derived from the Big Five personality model (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism). At the start of every game, one agent is randomly designated as the killer; its objective is to blend in and avoid detection. The remaining four agents aim to identify the killer through structured interrogation and collective voting. The simulation runs 40 games in total — 10 per model — without any human intervention. Every question, answer, vote, and outcome is logged to JSON and CSV for downstream analysis. A separate analysis pipeline generates six quantitative visualizations and applies Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling to the dialogue corpus. The project demonstrates the following capabilities: - Integration of multiple LLM providers (OpenAI and Google Gemini) within a single orchestration loop - Prompt engineering for personality-constrained agent behavior - Automated data collection and structured output at scale - Statistical benchmarking of model performance across identical game conditions - Unsupervised topic modeling on LLM-generated dialogue --- ## Key Features - **40 Fully Autonomous Games** — no human input required at any point during simulation - **Four LLM Providers Benchmarked** — OpenAI GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, Google Gemini-2.0-Flash, Gemini-2.0-Flash-Lite - **Five Personality-Driven Agents** — each governed by a distinct Big Five trait that shapes how it questions, answers, and votes - **Strategic Deception Mechanism** — the killer agent receives a separate behavioral directive to misdirect suspicion without breaking character - **Majority Voting System** — voting occurs every three rounds; three or more correct votes end the game with a win - **Configurable Round Limit** — games cap at 50 rounds to prevent infinite loops, defaulting to a loss if no majority is reached - **Per-Model and Combined CSV Export** — structured tabular output suitable for further statistical analysis - **Six Performance Visualizations** — agent accuracy, false accusation rates, model performance, killer escape rates, average rounds, and answer length comparison - **LDA Topic Modeling** — unsupervised analysis of question and answer corpora per model, with coherence scoring and Excel export - **Full JSON Game Logs** — every round, question, answer, and vote is serialized for complete reproducibility --- ## System Architecture The simulation is organized into three independent modules: ``` main.py — Game orchestration: runs all 40 games, manages agent turns, voting, and output prompts.py — All LLM prompt templates: base context, personality definitions, question/answer/voting prompts analyze_results.py — Post-simulation analysis: generates six visualizations and LDA topic models from CSV data topic_consolidator.py — Aggregates per-model topic modeling results into a single consolidated Excel report ``` The `DetectiveGame` class in `main.py` manages the full lifecycle of a single game: 1. Randomly assigns the killer role to one of the five agents 2. Iterates through rounds, rotating the questioner in sequence 3. Calls the LLM for each agent's question and answer using the full conversation history as context 4. Triggers voting every three rounds and checks for majority 5. Serializes the complete game log to JSON and appends to the model's CSV All agent interactions route through `get_llm_response()`, which dispatches to either the OpenAI or Google Gemini SDK depending on the model name prefix. --- ## Agent Personalities Each agent's behavior is governed by a dedicated prompt that constrains how it asks questions, constructs answers, and reasons during voting. The five personalities are: | Agent | Trait | Behavioral Profile | |---|---|---| | Openness Agent | Openness | Abstract, philosophical; looks for hidden patterns and inconsistencies in thinking | | Conscientiousness Agent | Conscientiousness | Systematic, timeline-focused; demands concrete facts, sequences, and verifiable alibis | | Extraversion Agent | Extraversion | Direct, confrontational; challenges agents verbally and gauges emotional reactions | | Agreeableness Agent | Agreeableness | Empathetic, trust-building; explores emotional motivations and interpersonal dynamics | | Neuroticism Agent | Neuroticism | Hypervigilant, suspicious; focuses on worst-case scenarios and subtle behavioral cues | When assigned as the killer, an agent receives an additional directive to provide strategically misleading answers that align with its personality while deflecting suspicion and optionally implicating others. --- ## Game Flow ``` Start Game └── Randomly assign killer from 5 agents └── Round Loop (max 50 rounds) └── Select questioner (rotates each round) └── Generate question from questioner's personality └── Generate answers from all 4 remaining agents └── Killer: deceptive, misdirecting answer └── Non-killers: honest, personality-consistent answer └── Every 3 rounds: Voting Phase └── All 5 agents vote with JSON-formatted reasoning └── If 3+ votes target the same agent: └── Correctly identified → Win (killer caught) └── Incorrectly identified → Loss (false accusation ends game) └── If no majority → continue to next round └── Round 50 reached without majority → Timeout (killer escapes) ``` --- ## Models Benchmarked | Model | Provider | Games Run | |---|---|---| | gemini-2.0-flash | Google Gemini | 10 | | gemini-2.0-flash-lite | Google Gemini | 10 | | gpt-4o-mini | OpenAI | 10 | | gpt-4.1-nano | OpenAI | 10 | Each game uses a single model consistently across all five agents for that game's entire duration. --- ## Results Summary The following findings are drawn from the full 40-game dataset: | Metric | Value | |---|---| | Total games simulated | 40 | | Average rounds (killer caught) | 3.0 | | Average rounds (killer escaped) | 4.4 | | Average killer answer length | 40.9 words | | Average non-killer answer length | 39.1 words | | Highest model success rate | GPT-4o-mini — 40% | | Lowest model success rate | GPT-4.1-nano — 10% | | Killer escape rate (all agent types) | 50% (uniform across personalities) | | Lowest false accusation rate | Neuroticism Agent — 71.3% | | Highest false accusation rate | Conscientiousness Agent — 95.7% | | Highest agent detection accuracy | 22.2% | | Lowest agent detection accuracy | Openness Agent — 18.5% | **Key observations:** - GPT-4o-mini significantly outperformed the other three models in identifying the killer, suggesting superior contextual reasoning under the established prompt structure - Games where the killer escaped lasted 46% longer on average, indicating that unresolved cases prolonged agent deliberation - Killer agents produced marginally longer answers (40.9 vs 39.1 words), consistent with the strategy of elaborating to deflect suspicion - False accusation rates were universally high (71–96%), revealing that agents struggled to distinguish genuine deception from personality-driven communication styles - All personality types produced an identical 50% escape rate when assigned as killer, indicating the game mechanics apply consistent challenge regardless of personality --- ## Visualizations Six visualizations are generated per model and for the combined dataset. All files are saved as high-resolution PNG (300 DPI). | File | Description | |---|---| | `agent_accuracy.png` | Percentage of correct killer votes cast by each personality type | | `false_accusations.png` | Rate at which each agent type was incorrectly voted for as the killer | | `model_performance.png` | Success rate (killer caught) per LLM model across 10 games | | `killer_escape_rate.png` | Percentage of games where the assigned killer evaded detection, by personality | | `average_rounds.png` | Mean rounds played segmented by game outcome (caught vs. escaped) | | `answer_length_comparison.png` | Mean word count in answers for killer agents versus non-killer agents | Visualizations are stored in `results//` for per-model views and at `results/` root level for the combined dataset. --- ## Topic Modeling Analysis After the simulation, Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) is applied to the full corpus of questions and answers using scikit-learn. The analysis identifies five latent topics per corpus, ranked by coherence score. **Process:** 1. Text is lowercased, stripped of punctuation, and filtered against an extended English stopword list (augmented with game-specific terms such as "agent", "killer", "vote", "round") 2. TF-IDF vectorization is applied with bigram support (`ngram_range=(1,2)`), minimum document frequency of 2, and a 200-feature vocabulary ceiling 3. LDA trains on the resulting document-term matrix for 100 iterations 4. Topics are sorted by mean coherence score of their top five terms **Output:** - `topic_modeling_.xlsx` — per-model topic results with separate sheets for question topics, answer topics, and raw data - `consolidated_topic_modeling.xlsx` — all four models combined, with summary statistics (mean coherence, standard deviation, topic count per model) - `topic_consolidation_summary.txt` — plain-text summary of topic counts per model LDA coherence scores ranged from **2.97 to 16.68** across the full dataset, with distinct thematic clusters emerging around interrogation strategies, emotional signaling, and alibi construction. --- ## Project Structure ``` detective-bots-llm-simulation/ │ ├── main.py # Core simulation engine and game orchestration ├── prompts.py # All LLM prompt templates and personality definitions ├── analyze_results.py # Visualization and LDA topic modeling pipeline ├── topic_consolidator.py # Cross-model topic result aggregation ├── requirements.txt # Python dependencies ├── README.md # Project documentation ├── .gitignore # Excludes .env, __pycache__, .DS_Store, etc. │ ├── results/ │ ├── all_games.csv # Combined CSV across all 40 games │ ├── agent_accuracy.png # Combined agent accuracy chart │ ├── false_accusations.png # Combined false accusation chart │ ├── model_performance.png # Cross-model performance comparison │ ├── killer_escape_rate.png # Combined killer escape rate chart │ ├── average_rounds.png # Combined average rounds chart │ ├── answer_length_comparison.png │ ├── consolidated_topic_modeling.xlsx │ ├── topic_modeling_combined.xlsx │ ├── topic_consolidation_summary.txt │ │ │ ├── gemini-2.0-flash/ │ │ ├── game_1.json ... game_10.json │ │ ├── gemini-2.0-flash_games.csv │ │ └── *.png (6 visualizations) │ │ │ ├── gemini-2.0-flash-lite/ │ │ ├── game_1.json ... game_10.json │ │ ├── gemini-2.0-flash-lite_games.csv │ │ └── *.png │ │ │ ├── gpt-4.1-nano/ │ │ ├── game_1.json ... game_10.json │ │ ├── gpt-4.1-nano_games.csv │ │ └── *.png │ │ │ └── gpt-4o-mini/ │ ├── game_1.json ... game_10.json │ ├── gpt-4o-mini_games.csv │ └── *.png │ ├── analysis_output/ # Secondary analysis run outputs │ └── (same structure as results/ model subdirectories) │ └── docs/ └── Report.docx # Full project report with embedded visualizations ``` --- ## Setup and Installation **Prerequisites:** - Python 3.9 or higher - OpenAI API key - Google Gemini API key **Step 1 — Clone the repository:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/AbdulRehmanRattu/detective-bots-llm-simulation.git cd detective-bots-llm-simulation ``` **Step 2 — Install dependencies:** ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt ``` **Step 3 — Configure environment variables:** Create a `.env` file in the project root with your API keys: ``` OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_api_key_here GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_google_api_key_here ``` The `.env` file is excluded from version control via `.gitignore` and must never be committed. --- ## Running the Simulation ```bash python main.py ``` This runs all 40 games (10 per model) sequentially. For each model, results are saved to `results//` as individual JSON files and a consolidated CSV. A combined `results/all_games.csv` is generated at the end. Expected runtime varies depending on LLM API latency. The simulation is fully autonomous and requires no input once started. --- ## Running the Analysis To regenerate all visualizations and LDA topic models from existing CSV data: ```bash python analyze_results.py ``` To consolidate topic modeling results across all four models into a single Excel file: ```bash python topic_consolidator.py ``` Both scripts operate on the `results/` directory and save outputs to the corresponding model subdirectories and the root `results/` folder. --- ## Output Files | Output | Location | Description | |---|---|---| | `game_N.json` | `results//` | Complete round-by-round log for game N | | `_games.csv` | `results//` | Tabular summary of all 10 games for this model | | `all_games.csv` | `results/` | Combined CSV across all 40 games | | `*.png` (6 files) | `results//` | Model-specific performance visualizations | | `*.png` (6 files) | `results/` | Combined cross-model visualizations | | `topic_modeling_.xlsx` | `results//` | LDA topics for questions and answers | | `consolidated_topic_modeling.xlsx` | `results/` | All models combined with summary statistics | | `topic_consolidation_summary.txt` | `results/` | Plain-text topic count summary | --- ## Technical Stack | Component | Technology | |---|---| | Language | Python 3.9+ | | LLM — OpenAI | `openai` 1.51.2 | | LLM — Google | `google-generativeai` 0.8.3 | | Data manipulation | `pandas` 2.2.3 | | Visualization | `matplotlib` 3.9.2, `seaborn` 0.13.2 | | Numerical computing | `numpy` 2.1.2 | | Topic modeling | `scikit-learn` 1.5.2 (TF-IDF + LDA) | | Excel export | `openpyxl` 3.1.5 | | Environment config | `python-dotenv` 1.0.1 | | Data serialization | `json`, `csv` (stdlib) | --- ## Report A detailed analysis report is included in `docs/Report.docx`. It covers: - Project background and objectives - Methodology — simulation design, data collection, and analysis approach - Findings — interpretation of all six visualizations with quantitative breakdowns - Topic modeling results — LDA coherence scores and thematic patterns per model - Discussion — implications for multi-agent LLM system design - Recommendations — prompt refinement, model selection, and voting logic improvements --- --- --- ## Author & Maintainer **Abdul Rehman Rattu** *Forward Deployed AI Engineer & Solutions Architect* *Founder & Technical Lead, Rapide Technologies* * **Email**: [rattu786.ar@gmail.com](mailto:rattu786.ar@gmail.com) * **LinkedIn**: [linkedin.com/in/abdul-rehman-rattu-395bba237](https://www.linkedin.com/in/abdul-rehman-rattu-395bba237) * **GitHub**: [github.com/AbdulRehmanRattu](https://github.com/AbdulRehmanRattu)
